SAFE Computation¶

class safe_vamd.safe_computation.SAFEComputation(source=None, backgrnd_field=None, mesh=None, acoustic_field=None, alpha_value=0.2, air_absorv=False, ground_impedance_value=None)¶

Bases: object

A class that represents an application of the Semi-Analytic Finite-Element (SAFE) method.

Class attributes:

source¶

An instance of Source with monopole source information.

Type:

Source

An instance of BackgroundField representing the atmospheric background field.

Type:

BackgroundField

Type:

‘Mesh1D’

complex

Parameters:

  • source (Source, optional) – An instance of Source with monopole source information.

  • backgrnd_field (BackgroundField, optional) – An instance of BackgroundField representing the atmospheric background field.

  • mesh (Mesh1D, optional) – An instance of Mesh1D with the finite-elements and nodes.

  • acoustic_field (AcousticField, optional) – An instance of AcousticField with the Vertical Atmospheric (VA) mode basis.

  • alpha_value (float, optional:) – A value to set added absorption in the Perfectly Matched Layer.

  • air_absorv (bool, optional) – A boolean to toggle air absorption (air_absorv = True) makes the computation take air absorption into account.

  • ground_impedance_value (complex, optional) – The complex-valued normalized surface ground impedance.

setup(input_file, f, rho_at_ground, g_value=9.81, pml_thick_factor=2)¶

Builds the objects related to the computational mesh and background atmospheric field from an inputted .txt file which has a header followed by columns for height (in \(m\)), temperature (in \(K\)), wind-velocity (in \(ms^{-1}\)) and relative humidity (in \(\%\)).

Parameters:

  • input_file (str) – Path to the input .txt file with the atmospheric conditions.

  • f (float) – Excitation frequency (in \(Hz\))

  • rho_at_ground (float) – Value of the air density (in \(kgm^{-3}\)) at ground level.

  • g_value (float, optional) – Value for the acceleration of gravity (in \(ms^{-2}\)).

  • pml_thick_factor (float, optional) – A unitless parameter that controls the thickness of the Perfectly Matched in proportion to the maximum wavelength.

Return type:

None

solve(ground_impedance_value=None, alpha_value=0.2, air_absorption=False)¶

Assembles the matrices for the cubic eigenvalue problem (:math:’A + Blambda + Clambda^2 +Dlambda^4’) and solves it by using the function kirby_solver_lagrange.

Parameters:

  • alpha_value (float) – A parameter to set added absorption in the Perfectly Matched Layer.

  • air_absorption (bool) – A boolean to toggle air absorption (air_absorv = True makes the simulation take into account air absorption) .

  • ground_impedance_value (complex) – The complex-valued normalized surface ground impedance.

Returns:

The acoustic pressure field with the upwind and downwind modes.

Return type:

AcousticField

match_to_monopole(source_height, source_amplitude, side='downwind')¶

Uses the methodology in https://doi.org/10.1121/10.0002912 to match either the upwind or downwind VA modes to a monopole source. it then updates the modal amplitudes on the AcousticField object.

Parameters:

  • source_height (float) – Height (in \(m\)) of the monopole.

  • source_amplitude (float) – Amplitude (in \(kgm^{-3}s^{-1}\)) of the monopole.

  • side (str) – Which set of modes should be used for the mode decomposition (side = “downwind” sets the procedure use the downwind modal set, “upwind” sets it to use the upwind modes).

Returns:

The acoustic field induced by the monopole.

Return type:

AcousticField

save_modes_in_txt()¶

Saves the upwind and downwind modes in separate .txt files with the save_modes_in_txt method in the acoustic_field attribute.

For \(K\) number of VA modes with eigenvectors of size .math:N, the .txt file has the following format:

\[\begin{split}\begin{matrix} z_1 & p_1(z_1) & \dots & p_K(z_1) \\ \dots & \dots & \dots & \dots \\ z_N & p_1(z_N) & \dots & p_K(z_N) \\ \hline \text{#} & A_1 & \dots & A_K \\ \text{#} & \lambda_1 & \dots & \lambda_K \\ \text{#} & k^{ref}_1 & \dots & k^{ref}_K \end{matrix}\end{split}\]

, where \(p_i(z_j)\) represents the vertical shape at height \(z_j\), \(A_i\) the mode amplitude, \(\lambda_i\) the eigenvalue, and \(k^{ref}_i\) the reference wavenumber for mode i. The symbol # represents irrelevant information in the .txt file.

Return type:

None
